text: It would be difficult to describe. <break time="0.8s" /> The quiet brotherhood of men. <break time="0.8s" /> That grew up in that boat. <break time="0.8s" /> For no one ever spoke of it. <break time="0.8s" /> The captain who could not row. <break time="0.8s" /> Gave orders in a soft voice. <break time="0.8s" /> And the three men obeyed him. <break time="0.8s" /> More willingly than any crew had ever done. <break time="0.8s" /> The correspondent who had been taught to doubt people. <break time="0.8s" /> Felt even then. <break time="0.8s" /> That this was the best experience of his life. <break time="0.8s" /> Later the men raised. <break time="0.8s" /> The captains overcoat on an oar. <break time="0.8s" /> As a little sail. <break time="0.8s" /> And the boat moved more easily. <break time="0.8s" /> Toward the shore. <break time="0.8s" /> Someone found eight cigars. <break time="0.8s" /> Four of them still dry. <break time="0.8s" /> And the men smoked them proudly. <break time="0.8s" /> And drank some fresh water. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon they could see. <break time="0.8s" /> The low, dark line of land. <break time="0.8s" /> But there was no life saving station. <break time="0.8s" /> On the shore. <break time="0.8s" /> And no boat came out. <break time="0.8s" /> The surf was so rough. <break time="0.8s" /> That the captain decided. <break time="0.8s" /> They must row back out to sea. <break time="0.8s" /> And wait. <break time="0.8s" /> If I am going to be drowned. <break time="0.8s" /> The correspondent thought angrily. <break time="0.8s" /> Why was I allowed. <break time="0.8s" /> To come so far. <break time="0.8s" /> And see sand and trees.
